chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Ibn Bukayr and Yahya ibn al-Muthanna, from al-Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, for the Qa'im (the Rising One) are two occultations; he returns in one of them, but in the latter, it is not known where he is. He attends the seasons (of pilgrimage), he sees the people but they do not see him.

key_terms.الْمَوَاسِمَ: The seasons (specifically referring to Hajj seasons)
key_terms.لِلْقَائِمِ: The Rising One (referring to the Twelfth Imam)
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: He returns (implies re-emergence or visibility in the first)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of the Imam al-Qa'im and how does he attend the Hajj seasons?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* delineates the two phases of the Twelfth Imam’s occultation, distinguishing the Lesser Occultation (Ghaybat al-Sughra) where he was accessible via deputies, from the Greater Occultation (Ghaybat al-Kubra) where his precise location remains hidden from the general public. It highlights the theological concept of the Imam’s continuous presence among the faithful, specifically noting his invisible attendance at Hajj pilgrimages, which serves as a source of spiritual reassurance (tawassul) for the Shia community during the period of waiting (intizar).
